description: Working with video as a first-class object: importing and generating video, extracting and mapping over frames, trimming, joining and splitting, transcoding, and building videos from computed frames or animations.

tools.name: Video
tools.description: Represents a video, constructed from a file, URL or list of frames, with audio tracks preserved. It displays as an interactive player and works with a large family of video functions. Video is handled lazily, so large files are not loaded entirely into memory.

parameters.name: FrameRate
parameters.description: Frames per second of the video.

tools.notes: Import["clip.mp4"] also returns a Video object; Information gives codec, size and stream details.

tools.name: VideoQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid Video object. It is the type guard for video-processing code and pattern definitions. Use it to branch safely on input type.

tools.name: VideoFrameList
tools.description: Returns a list of frames sampled from a video, either a given number spread evenly or frames at specified times. Frames come back as Image objects ready for processing. Use it for thumbnails, analysis and dataset creation.
tools.notes: VideoExtractFrames returns frames from a time interval rather than a sampled selection.

tools.name: VideoExtractFrames
tools.description: Extracts all frames of a video within a specified time interval or at specified times. Unlike VideoFrameList it is aimed at dense extraction rather than sampling. Use it when you need every frame of a segment.

tools.name: VideoFrameMap
tools.description: Applies a function to every frame of a video and returns a new video built from the results. Processing is streamed, so very long videos can be handled. Use it for filtering, annotation and per-frame analysis.
tools.notes: VideoMap and VideoMapList operate on time intervals and return videos or lists respectively.

tools.name: VideoMap
tools.description: Applies a function to successive time intervals of a video, producing a new video. It gives access to a window of frames at a time rather than a single frame. Use it for temporal filtering, motion analysis and effects that need context.

tools.name: VideoMapList
tools.description: Applies a function to successive intervals of a video and returns the results as a list rather than a video. It is the analysis counterpart of VideoMap. Use it to compute per-interval features such as brightness or motion energy.

tools.name: VideoTrim
tools.description: Extracts a time segment from a video, keeping audio in sync. Times may be given in seconds, as Quantity values or as frame numbers. It is the basic cutting operation for video editing.

tools.name: VideoSplit
tools.description: Splits a video into segments at specified times or according to detected scene changes. The result is a list of Video objects. Use it to break long recordings into shots or chapters.

tools.name: VideoJoin
tools.description: Concatenates videos end to end, transcoding as needed so that frame rates and sizes match. Audio tracks are joined along with the video. Use it to assemble clips into a single output.
tools.notes: VideoCombine overlays videos and audio simultaneously instead of concatenating them.

tools.name: VideoCombine
tools.description: Combines several videos and audio objects into one by playing them together, mixing tracks rather than concatenating. Layout and alignment options control how visual streams are arranged. Use it to add a soundtrack or build side-by-side comparisons.

tools.name: VideoInsert
tools.description: Inserts one video, image or audio object into another at a specified time. It shifts the remaining content later rather than overwriting it. Use it to splice in title cards or additional footage.
tools.notes: VideoDelete removes a time interval instead of adding one.

tools.name: VideoDelete
tools.description: Removes a specified time interval from a video, closing the gap. It is the complement of VideoInsert. Use it to cut out unwanted segments without re-exporting manually.

tools.name: VideoTranscode
tools.description: Converts a video to a different container, codec, resolution, frame rate or bit rate. It is the main tool for preparing video for a target platform. Many parameters can be changed in a single call.

tools.name: VideoTimeStretch
tools.description: Changes the playback speed of a video by a given factor, optionally keeping audio pitch correct. Frame interpolation can be used for smooth slow motion. Use it for speed ramps and time-lapse effects.

tools.name: VideoGenerator
tools.description: Generates synthetic test video of a given duration, useful for testing pipelines without real footage. Resolution, frame rate and content type can be specified. Use it for reproducible examples and benchmarks.

tools.name: AnimationVideo
tools.description: Renders an animation defined by an expression varying over a parameter into a Video object. It is the video equivalent of Animate and Table over frames. Use it to produce shareable animations of plots and simulations.
tools.usage:
AnimationVideo[expr, {t, tmin, tmax}]
AnimationVideo[expr, iter, opts]
tools.notes: FrameListVideo builds a video from an explicit list of images; SlideShowVideo makes a slideshow with per-frame durations.

tools.name: FrameListVideo
tools.description: Creates a video from an explicit list of images or graphics, at a chosen frame rate. It is the most direct way to turn computed frames into a video file. Use it after generating frames in a loop.

tools.name: SlideShowVideo
tools.description: Builds a video slideshow from a list of images, each shown for a specified duration, with optional transitions. It is convenient for presentations and time-stamped image sequences. Audio can be combined afterwards with VideoCombine.

tools.name: TourVideo
tools.description: Creates a video that moves a virtual camera through a 3D scene or across an image along a specified path. It automates smooth fly-throughs and pans. Use it to present 3D models and large images dynamically.

tools.name: VideoScreenCapture
tools.description: Records the screen, a window or a region into a Video object. Recording can be stopped programmatically or after a set duration. Use it to capture interactive sessions and demonstrations.
tools.notes: Requires screen-recording permission on some operating systems.

tools.name: VideoRecord
tools.description: Records video from a connected camera device into a Video object. Duration, resolution and device can be specified. Use it for live capture inside notebooks and automated acquisition.

tools.name: VideoStream
tools.description: Creates a controllable playback stream for a video, allowing programmatic play, pause and seeking. It gives finer control than the default player. Use it in interactive applications and synchronized displays.

tools.name: VideoIntervals
tools.description: Finds time intervals in a video where a given criterion holds, such as silence, motion or a custom frame predicate. It returns a list of time ranges. Use it to locate scenes of interest automatically.

tools.name: VideoSummaryPlot
tools.description: Produces an overview visualization of a video showing sampled frames, audio waveform and timeline information. It is a quick way to understand the structure of a clip. Use it before deciding how to segment or process the video.
